### From Protestant to Orthodox

Protestants and particularly evangelicals take a 'minimalist' approach to Salvation. They focus on Salvation as justification: 'I can go to heaven rather than hell.' Plenty of people think that is all there is to it - 'Just accept Jesus as your savior'.

#### The Baptist Experience

I was a Baptist for many years, taught that Scripture alone must be our guide. Any traditions not explicitly found in the Bible were seen as 'traditions of men'. Our calling was 'to get back to the New Testament Church'.

#### The Discovery of Diversity

In missions, I found great diversity of opinion on 'what the Bible clearly taught' - issues like baptism (symbol vs. salvation), infant baptism, once saved always saved, and church government. All had support in Scripture, but no one could prove conclusively what the 'original Church' believed using only the New Testament.

#### Conclusion

The Orthodox Church has been the ultimate revelation of what it means to be 'in Christ'. My upbringing in Evangelical Protestantism was preparing me for this all along.
